decisions.mark: distinguishes the two ways to substitute an allocator — a COMPILE-time pair of macros versus a RUNTIME pair of function pointers — and states that they are mutually exclusive
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "Option A, compile time. Define both macros in your user config... Option B, runtime. Define only `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, then call `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free(my_calloc, my_free)`... The macros take precedence over the runtime setter, and `platform.c` drops its pointer code entirely in that case." | WHY: It distinguishes the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer pair, and says the macros drop the pointer code entirely, so the two are exclusive in effect. The word "exclusive" never appears, though. || QUOTE: "Option A, compile time. Define both macros in your user config... Option B, runtime. Define only `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, then call `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free(my_calloc, my_free)`... The macros take precedence over the runtime setter, and `platform.c` drops its pointer code entirely in that case." | WHY: The answer separates a compile-time macro pair from a runtime function-pointer pair. It says the macros override the runtime setter and remove the pointer code, which makes the two mechanisms mutually exclusive.

decisions.mark: identifies the buffer allocator (MBEDTLS_MEMORY_BUFFER_ALLOC_C) as the only in-tree user of the runtime setter, installing itself over the pointers from its init function
